population.label: Caucasian (European background; used for Australian patients of European background)

curation.notes: Ruling P23: one set per McNamara sample. Ruling P24: Burlington (Table IV) compared as mcnamara1984-burlington.a.json against the Table IV rows of mcnamara1984-caucasian.b.json (script comparison 2026-10-08, positive control: two planted changes found): 56 rows, 0 differences in mean, SD and n. Every value re-read on the page image (PDF p. 6 = p. 454): agrees, including the men's two-decimal SDs (3.83, 4.15, 5.11, 5.70, 5.97, 6.00). Differential printed without SD ('—') -> no sd. Girls' Co-A 88.3 at 9 y and 87.3 at 12 y as printed, noted (merge notes). Selection unknown: p. 450 describes them only as normal children of the Burlington Orthodontic Research Centre, also followed over time, and gives no criteria (a: random-unselected; b: class-I-balanced for the paper as a whole) -> unknown, the merge notes' default. n per age and sex from the table. Scale enlarged 8% (p. 451; heading 'standardized 8% enlargement').

caveats: 'Caucasian' is our label: the paper never states the samples' ethnicity (it says nothing about ancestry).

Normal children of the Burlington Orthodontic Research Centre, also followed over time (p. 450); the paper gives no selection criteria and no whole-sample count (the n per age and sex in Table IV run from 17 to 58).

8% film enlargement: p. 451 says the measures from all these samples include an 8% enlargement wherever possible; the table heading says 'standardized 8% enlargement'. The app shows mm values at true size (÷ 1.08) with the printed value.
Values are printed at single ages (6, 9, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 y). A child between two printed ages gets the nearest printed age, marked as not his age (no interpolation is used for this set).
The maxillomandibular differential is printed without an SD; it borrows one at display, said in the line.
Girls' midfacial length (Co-point A) is printed 88.3 at 9 y and 87.3 at 12 y, a fall against the trend; as printed.
Some values fall from 18 to 20 y (e.g. women's Co-Gn 118.9 at 18 y, n 22, and 116.8 at 20 y, n 44); the n differ by age, so the groups at each age are not all the same children. As printed.
